newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain Renfe withBCH to buy Retevision - press.
newsitem.headline: Spain Renfe withBCH to buy Retevision - press.

text.p: The Spanish railways operator Renfe made on Sunday a deal with the consortium headed by Banco Central Hispano to buy Retevision, the newspaper El Pais reported on Monday.
Both Renfe and BCH were not immediately available to make comments on the report.
Today is the first deadline to show interest in the 60 percent offer of Retevision, the Spanish second basic telephone operator.
According to the report, Renfe would be interested to make available its fiber optic network to the consortium.
This consortium comprises of Banco Central Hispano, France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom.
The Retevision stake is due to be sold by mid-year. The firm will have the ambitious task of competing with the recently-privatised domestic operator Telefonica.
At mid-March, Retevision's board approved the conditions for the sale of a 60 percent stake in the firm for a minimum price of 45.6 billion pesetas.
The bidder will be obliged to underwrite a 10 percent capital increase in the firm, with a further payment of 25.33 billion pesetas.

Apart from the BCH consortium, Endesa has said it is likely to be involved in the Retevision auction and press reports today linked the electricity firm with the Italian operator Stet to present a second offer.
The period for presentation of bids ends on June 9, and the auction will be resolved in 60 days.
Retevision hopes to provide an alternative to Telefonica's services in Spain before the end of the year.
